prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its development into incretin therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six openings ranked B046 first, and I still think that is right on the merits rather than because of the tally. GLP-1 work runs from the physiology of the gut hormone and its secretion (Holst), through the biology of proglucagon-derived peptides and receptor actions (Drucker), to long-acting analogues that now have randomized outcome data in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease (Knudsen). It is a single coherent arc from basic physiology to a major medicine, confirmed independently over decades, so it is neither premature nor contested on the science. A prize that credits the physiology and the translation together fits the Physiology or Medicine remit well.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is real: four names are supplied, the cap is three, and the early peptide identification and synthesis work (Mojsov, and the Habener group outside the supplied names) is left out of my trio. A reasonable committee could weigh the basic-science side more heavily and drop the industrial developer. There is also a risk that a prize this expected looks like a clinical-impact award rather than a discovery award, and long-term safety of chronic incretin therapy is still accumulating.

responses.point: Proposes Drucker, Holst and Mojsov for B046, treating Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1 form as part of the discovery core and Knudsen's industrial development as secondary.
responses.response: This is the strongest challenge to my trio and I take it seriously. If the prize is framed as discovery of the incretin hormone, Mojsov belongs in it. My concern is that without Knudsen the citation cannot honestly cover the therapeutic half, which is what most of the clinical and public-health impact rests on, and our remit values the physiology-to-patient arc. Unless someone shows the peptide-identification priority is decisive and well documented, I keep Knudsen, but I would accept a Mojsov-for-Knudsen swap if the committee frames B046 as a discovery prize, and I regard the question as open.

responses.point: Ranks B037 and then B021 (TNF blockade) after GLP-1, stressing that anti-TNF is fully mature and arguably overdue, and that CAR-T attribution is complicated by Eshhar.
responses.response: I agree that TNF blockade is mature and clinically broad, but it ranks below CAR-T for me because the conceptual originality is smaller: the target and antibody modality were comparatively established by the time the trials proved efficacy. I share your Eshhar concern about CAR-T, and it is why I would not put B037 above B046. On your point about allocation between basic physiologists and developers in B046, I think the answer is to credit both rather than exclude the developer.

responses.point: Ranks the unfolded protein response (B014) second as a conceptually complete new signalling logic with a clean Walter and Mori pairing, ahead of CAR-T.
responses.response: The UPR attribution is cleaner than CAR-T, and I agree the mechanism is original and mature. I placed it fourth because its disease relevance is still largely inferred rather than shown in patients, whereas CAR-T gives durable remissions today. This is a genuine difference of weighting, not a scientific disagreement, and I would not object if the committee decided clean attribution outweighs clinical proof; that is why I keep B014 as an alternative.

responses.point: Ranks optogenetics (B030) second as exceptional methodology that changed causal circuit neuroscience, and CAR-T fourth.
responses.response: I rank optogenetics third and I will say plainly that its field overlaps with my own, so I discount any pull I feel toward it. Even setting that aside, six credited names against a three-person cap, with live priority disputes over Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck, make a defensible trio hard to find, and its clinical benefit is still early. I do not think it can compete with B046 this year, though I accept it may in the future.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov should replace Knudsen (or Drucker or Holst) is unresolved and depends on a priority record I have not independently verified.
Whether the committee wants a physiology-led or a drug-development-led citation for B046.
Whether CAR-T (B037) can be given a defensible three-person attribution given Eshhar's foundational chimeric receptor work.
Whether the committee wants to pair a second distinct achievement with B046 or keep a single-part prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B046, B037 or B014. My profile lists a 2009 co-authored paper with Thomas Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons, which does not involve the candidates I propose. My research field (motor-circuit neuroscience) is adjacent to optogenetics (B030), but I am not proposing it.
